tasks.task: Read a till or POS export and write a sales readout

items.when: When the owner sends a till export and wants best lines, dead hours and basket size on one page
When the owner asks a question the standard readout does not answer, such as a trend or a link
When the numbers are in, to size whether more buyers, bigger baskets or more repeat visits pays most
When sales fell against last month, to find which number moved and what to check next
Before the readout goes to the owner, to catch broken formulas and totals that do not add up
When the report says what sold but nobody has asked staff and customers why

tasks.task: Run the Monday trading review

items.when: Every Monday, before deliveries and the rota are fixed, to turn last week into this week's actions
When the review needs last week's sales, margin and busy hours from the till export
When the review must also say what to reorder and whether the cash is there to pay for it
Once a month, to put sales and costs in four buckets and see which line to fix first

tasks.task: Build a 12-month promotions calendar

items.when: When the shop needs a year of promotions tied to its busy and quiet weeks, each with one goal
When past deals exist, to size the lift of each promotion and the extra stock to hold
When every idea is a price cut, to get gift, bundle and pre-order promotions to compare
When the owner must choose between a few big events and a steady monthly rhythm
When a promotion is a prize draw, a competition or a claim that local rules may limit

tasks.task: Plan one sale or offer and check the margin

items.when: Before a sale, to find the deepest discount the margin allows and the wording to use
When a multi-buy or bundle might lift the basket more than a straight price cut
When the offer needs a real end date or stock limit and the words to state it truthfully
When several offers run at once, to catch discounts that clash or confuse at the till
When the only lever anyone suggests is a bigger discount

tasks.task: Write window and in-store sign copy

items.when: When a promotion is agreed and you need the window line, shelf cards and till sign for it
When the window line is flat, to get five short headlines that each take a different angle
When the owner wants to see three different looks for the sign set at real size before printing
When a sign shows a full price and a sale price and you want the clearest honest form
When a line could hang in any shop, to test it and get a true rewrite a passer-by can picture
When the sign is laid out, to see what the eye hits first from the pavement and what to cut
When the owner will print the signs themselves and needs a template they can reuse

tasks.task: Check price claims, sale signs and returns notices

items.when: Before printing a was/now price, a last-few sign, a green claim or a returns notice
When a sign leans on scarcity or a deadline, to see which claims are true and rewrite the rest
When you are unsure which consumer rules apply where the shop trades, to list them and the gaps
When the returns notice is unclear because the shop has never set its refund rules

tasks.task: Plan an in-store event and its run sheet

items.when: When the shop wants a late opening, workshop, signing or tasting to fill a quiet day
Before committing, to set the event up as a small test with costs, measures and a decision rule
When the event is a tasting, to plan the day, a taster card and how to read the result
When the workshop or class is ticketed and needs a price and early-bird terms
When the event needs a poster for the window with checked text and an export checklist
After the event, to follow up with people who came and keep each promise made on the night

tasks.task: Write a staff selling guide and five-minute briefing

items.when: When staff wait at the till while people browse, add-on sales are low or a new person starts
When staff freeze on the first line, to get a ten-word opener, two spares and a way to test them
When customers raise the same doubts about price or quality and staff need an answer for each
When staff describe products instead of letting the customer hold, try or taste them

tasks.task: Build next week's rota from the busy hours

items.when: When you need next week's rota with cover following the busy hours and breaks checked
When you want two or three rota options, each with a cover and wage cost check, before you publish
When weekends and late nights fall on the same people and you need a fair rotation and swap rule
When a shift pattern raises a break, overtime or rest question for the place you trade

tasks.task: Plan and run a stock count and work out shrink

items.when: When a full or cycle count is due and you need count sheets, the reconcile and shrink by cause
When setting the year's rhythm: one or two full counts with rolling cycle counts in between
When you need a rolling schedule of what gets counted when and who counts it
When the count and the record disagree, to split timing, unit and counting errors before blaming theft
When shrink is high and the shop needs opening, closing, cash and stock-loss routines written down

tasks.task: Plan reorders and a seasonal stock buy

items.when: When you need reorder points, safety stock and an ABC ranking from stock and sales numbers
Before a season, to decide how much to buy early, how much to hold back and when to mark down
When an item sells once, such as Christmas cards, and you must pick one order quantity
Before placing a big order, to see true unit costs and whether the cash covers it
When reordering should become a weekly routine from the stock and sales export

tasks.task: Clear slow stock with a markdown plan

items.when: Before marking anything down, to sort stock by how long it has sat unsold
When slow lines must go, to set when and how deep to cut so they sell out
When a gift-with-purchase or bundle could shift the stock without a red sticker
After the markdown, to check units sold, units left and cash recovered against what the stock cost

tasks.task: Plan a pop-up or market stall: break-even, stock and float

items.when: When a market, fair or pop-up is booked or offered and you need the sums, stock list and float
When you want every step from the booking decision to the review after the event in order
When you cannot restock mid-event and must choose how much of each line to bring
When there are two ways to run the stall, such as few hero lines or the full range, to compare both

tasks.task: Plan a stall or shop-floor layout and display

items.when: When you need the stall plan: table, height, price signs and where the customer stands and pays
When shelf space is tight and best sellers and high-margin lines should get the best positions
When first-time visitors cannot find a section, the till or the fitting room
When the stall banner and price cards need a look, to compare three directions at real size
Before the price cards are printed, to check every price and claim on them

tasks.task: Write a market or craft fair application

items.when: When applying for a pitch and the organiser asks who you are, what you sell and why you fit
When the one-line description of the stall is dull, to try five angles on it
When the description sounds like every other maker, to get a true, picturable rewrite
Before sending, to read the application as the organiser choosing between fifty stalls

tasks.task: Review sales after a pop-up, market or event

items.when: After the event, to compare takings with the break-even and decide whether to book again
When the event sales came through the till or card reader and need reading by line and hour

tasks.task: Set shelf prices and how they are shown

items.when: When prices must be set against costs and nearby rivals, with a rule for answering their discounts
When choosing between a round price and one just below it for a given product
After a price change, to see what it did to margin across the shop

tasks.task: Design a loyalty or best-customer programme

items.when: When the shop has purchase history and wants a best-customer profile, perks and personal touches
When you want tier designs with perks that are not discounts, plus a test
Before launch, to test what the scheme costs against who it really reaches

tasks.task: Plan local marketing: listing, reviews, email and text

items.when: When the owner does not know where new customers could come from, to compare channels and pick tests
When the shop is hard to find on maps, to audit the listing and plan fixes and more reviews
When the shop needs a routine for asking happy customers for reviews and answering bad ones
When the shop has an email list and wants an issue made from shop news and customer questions
When a sale should be announced to the list by email and text with a send calendar

tasks.task: Handle returns and complaints at the counter

items.when: When a return arrives, to check it against the policy, work out the refund and draft a kind reply
When the shop has no clear returns rules and staff decide each case on the spot
When an angry message arrives and the reply must fix what it can and promise nothing false
Before a complaint reply goes out, to check every promise in it can be kept

tasks.task: Write opening, closing and cash-up procedures

items.when: When the till is often out and the shop needs opening, closing and cash check steps for review
When the owner's standards live in their head and each role needs a job card
When a second site or a manager is coming and a stranger must be able to run the shop from the manual
When the shop runs differently depending on who opened up that morning

tasks.task: Compare supplier quotes and ask for better terms

items.when: When two or more suppliers quote, to see price, minimum order, lead time and risk side by side
When the shop wants longer payment terms or sale-or-return and needs a fair ask
When the supplier is far bigger than the shop and the owner dreads the call

always.when: Before any sign, guide or application is printed or sent, to catch typos and mixed-up names
When a sign or post states a number, an origin or an award you cannot trace to the shop's records

helpers.when: When signs, posters, price cards or a stall banner must be laid out and made print-ready
When the job is being found locally: map listing, reviews and neighbourhood promotion
When the promotion or event needs a posting plan, not only signs in the window
When an event has ticketing, suppliers or licences beyond a simple in-store evening
When the stock value, cash-up or till totals must tie to the books for the accountant
When prices across the whole range need rethinking, not one sale

gaps: No library item reads a physical shop's till export from Square, Shopify POS or Lightspeed; the fits read online store data
No library item plans a window display or shop-floor visual merchandising beyond shelf facings
No library item plans a market stall layout: table, height, price signs and customer flow
No library item works out a cash float, a cash-up routine or a till variance for a shop or stall
No library item writes a market, craft fair or pop-up space application
No library item checks was/now prices, last-few signs and returns notices against consumer rules by country
No library item writes a shop-floor selling guide with greetings, add-on prompts and role-plays
No library item splits shrink into theft, damage, admin error and supplier short delivery for a small shop
No library item checks a rota against local rules on breaks, rest, young workers and shift notice
No library item works out break-even for a market pitch from fees, travel, staff and stock cost
No library item measures footfall and the share of visitors who buy in a physical shop
